record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can federated optimization algorithms be designed specifically for federated constraints such as non-IID and unbalanced data, limited communication bandwidth, unreliable availability, client sampling, stateless cross-device clients, and compatibility with privacy and secure aggregation mechanisms?

evidence.quote: target the characteristics of the federated learning setting

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning system consisting of a central coordinator (server) and a population of $N$ clients indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$, where each client $i$ holds a local data distribution $\mathcal{D}_i$ over an input space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$. For a parameter vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a loss function $\ell:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$, define the local objective $F_i(w) := \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}_i}[\ell(w;x,y)]$ and the global federated objective
$$F(w) := \sum_{i=1}^N p_i F_i(w), \qquad \sum_{i=1}^N p_i = 1,\; p_i \ge 0.$$
A federated optimization algorithm is an iterative procedure in which, at each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the server selects a (possibly random) subset $S_t \subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$ of clients, broadcasts state to those clients, each selected client $i \in S_t$ performs local computation on its data and returns a message $m_{i,t}$ to the server, and the server aggregates the messages to update $w_t$.

The algorithm must operate under the following federated constraints simultaneously:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(C1)] \emph{Non-IID and unbalanced data}: the distributions $\mathcal{D}_i$ may differ arbitrarily across clients, and the effective sample sizes may vary widely.
\item[(C2)] \emph{Limited communication bandwidth}: there is a fixed upper bound $B$ on the number of bits exchanged per client per round.
\item[(C3)] \emph{Unreliable availability and client sampling}: at each round only a small random subset of clients is available, governed by an availability process possibly correlated with $i$ and $t$.
\item[(C4)] \emph{Stateless cross-device clients}: each client may participate at most once (or very few times) and cannot maintain persistent state between rounds; the algorithm cannot rely on client-side memory across rounds.
\item[(C5)] \emph{Compatibility with secure aggregation and privacy}: server-side updates must be computable from sums (or otherwise privacy-preserving aggregates) of client messages, so that the server learns only the aggregate and not individual $m_{i,t}$, and the procedure must support a differential-privacy guarantee with parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$.
\end{enumerate}

Question: Design a federated optimization algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ satisfying all of (C1)–(C5) that, for the class of (possibly nonconvex) smooth objectives, provably converges to an $\epsilon$-stationary point of $F$ (i.e., $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla F(\hat w)\|^2 \le \epsilon$) with communication, sampling, and privacy complexities that improve over (or at least match) the best known bounds for centralized stochastic optimization adapted naively to the federated setting. Equivalently: characterize the achievable trade-offs between convergence rate, per-round communication cost, client participation rate, statelessness, and privacy parameters under constraints (C1)–(C5), and exhibit an algorithm that attains these trade-offs.
artifact.status_search_result: Federated optimization under the combined constraints of non-IID data, communication efficiency, partial participation, statelessness, and privacy/secure-aggregation compatibility remains an active and broadly open research direction. While many partial results exist (e.g., FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedOpt, and various compressed/DP variants address subsets of the constraints), no single algorithm with matching lower-bound-tight guarantees under all of (C1)–(C5) simultaneously has been established as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems in designing federated optimization algorithms targeting non-IID data, limited communication, unreliable client availability, and compatibility with privacy/secure aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open direction in the federated learning research agenda.

status_evidence.title: A Field Guide to Federated Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys federated optimization algorithms and notes ongoing challenges in handling heterogeneity, partial participation, and privacy simultaneously.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent surveys continue to list these as open challenges, indicating no comprehensive solution.
